item.title: A Skeptic’s Guide to Ozempic and Other GLP-1 Agonists
item.description: William Meller, MD, examines the GLP-1 drug phenomenon. Are these “miracle” weight loss drugs worth the hype, or just expensive lifetime prescriptions with serious trade-offs? The surprising science and sobering risks revealed.

item.title: Scientific Inconsistencies in the Quran: A Greater Challenge Than Its Violent Verses?
item.description: Ex-Muslim author Majid Oukacha argues that scientific contradictions in the Quran—mathematical impossibilities in inheritance laws, verbatim quote mismatches—are more effective tools for challenging faith than critiques of violence. Facts trump subjectivity when scripture claims divine perfection.

item.title: CRISPR-Cas9 and the Ethics of Scientific Inaction
item.description: Discover how CRISPR could save the Everglades from ecological collapse—without mass killing. As Burmese pythons devastate 90% of mammal populations, scientists deploy robotic rabbits while rejecting the one tool that might actually work. Why is precision considered riskier than failure?

item.title: Dice, Mr. Smith, and Monty: The Case for Clarity in Probability Puzzles
item.description: Think you know probability? Stephanie Simoes reveals how vague framing and hidden assumptions lead even experts astray. This sharp, accessible piece reveals why the information-generating process changes everything—and why two people can give contradictory answers and both be right.

item.title: Ufology: From Fringe to Mainstream to Fringe?
item.description: Former UK Ministry of Defence UFO investigator Nick Pope traces how ufology moved from conspiracy theory to Congressional hearings after the 2017 New York Times revelations. He then examines the infighting, whistleblowers, and quasi-religious narratives threatening to push it back to the fringe.
